definitions.explanation: A vitamin, mineral, or herbal product taken to make up for something missing in the diet. Short for サプリメント, and the form used in ordinary conversation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧サプリ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}んでいる→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧{不足|ぶそく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧サプリ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{補|おぎな}っている→補う：00329_oginau⟧。
examples.english: I'm making up for my lack of vegetables with supplements.

examples.japanese: サプリ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦あくまで→あくまで：06713_akumade⟧⟦{補助|ほじょ}→補助：14105_hojo⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦まず→まず：00796_mazu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見直|みなお}した→見直す：04579_minaosu⟧⟦ほうがいい→ほうがいい：10078_hougaii⟧。
examples.english: Supplements are only a supplement, so you should start by reviewing your diet.

notes:
A clipping of サプリメント (from English "supplement"). Japanese frequently shortens four-mora-plus loanwords this way; the long form survives on packaging and in advertising.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サプリ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧: to take a supplement (⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧, not ⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧)
- サプリ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{補|おぎな}う→補う：00329_oginau⟧: to make up for something with supplements
- ⟦{鉄分|てつぶん}→鉄分：19444_tetsubun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧サプリ: an iron supplement
- ⟦{健康|けんこう}→健康：02706_kenkou⟧サプリ: a health supplement

USAGE:
Note the verb: pills and capsules are ⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧ in Japanese even when swallowed without water. The commonest frame in conversation is 〜{不足|ぶそく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧サプリ⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{補|おぎな}う→補う：00329_oginau⟧.
